page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs using hyperthreading. It includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. Cache architecture is composed of a 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (foundation and VNNI), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI for cryptographic and vector tasks. The instance does not feature local storage or GPU acceleration, requiring networked block storage for persistent filesystem needs.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within average performance thresholds across CPU and memory tests. The E16s_v4 records a PassMark CPU score of 15546.06 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8567.0. The memory subsystem sustains 96.64 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 55.64 GB/sec write bandwidth on large blocks, driving 12.92 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 5319.93. Bottlenecks appear in single-threaded bzip3 decompression (8.63 GB/sec) and medium 7B model LLM prompt processing (24.19 tokens/sec), both placing in the lower 25th percentile.

Cost efficiency is tied directly to high memory density relative to compute resources, reducing per-gigabyte provisioning overhead for memory-bound applications without unneeded expenditure on bundled local disks. A primary operational tradeoff is reliance on external storage, making I/O performance dependent on remote disk configuration. The instance is suited for relational databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, in-memory analytics, and data pipeline processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E16s_v4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores on x86_64 architecture, clocked at 2.8 GHz. The configuration supplies 128.0 GB of RAM, representing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio, backed by 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction capabilities. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, functioning as a diskless node reliant on external networked storage. Synthetic testing places overall system performance in the average band, marked by 96.64 GB/sec large-block uncached memory read bandwidth and 12.92 million Redis SET operations per second, with weaker results in single-threaded decompression. The instance offers resource efficiency for RAM-heavy deployments without the operational cost of local SSDs. Workload fit includes in-memory databases, memory caching tiers, relational database engines, and enterprise backend applications.
